title: Canh Chua Cá: Sour Fish Soup with Snapper, Tomato and Pineapple
summary: A quick, bright canh chua with chunks of white fish, a cooked-down tomato base, tamarind and lime, pineapple and okra, topped with bean sprouts, spring onion and coriander.

ingredients.item: skinless snapper or other firm white fish fillet, in 4 cm chunks
ripe tomato, finely chopped, plus 2 more cut into wedges
okra pods, cut in thick pieces

steps.title: Prepare the fish
steps.text: Toss the fish chunks with the 1 tsp fish sauce and set aside while you start the base.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in the saucepan over medium heat. Fry the shallots and garlic for 2 min until soft, add the chopped tomato and cook 4-5 min, pressing with the spoon, until it collapses into a thick red sauce.

steps.title: Build the broth
steps.text: Pour in the water, bring to the boil, then stir in the tamarind, sugar and the 1.5 tbsp fish sauce. Simmer 5 min.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the pineapple and okra and simmer 3 min.

steps.title: Poach the fish
steps.text: Lower the heat so the broth barely bubbles. Add the fish and the tomato wedges and cook 4-5 min without stirring hard, until the fish is opaque and flakes (63 °C in the centre).

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust with a pinch of sugar or a little more lime.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Put bean sprouts in each bowl, ladle in the soup and scatter with spring onion and coriander. Eat with steamed rice.

tips: Cook the chopped tomato right down first; it gives the broth body and colour.
Keep the broth just trembling once the fish is in so the chunks stay whole.
Add the lime off the heat so it stays fresh-tasting.
storage: Eat on the day. Leftovers keep 1 day in the fridge; reheat gently until steaming hot. Not suitable for freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
